question:
**Case Study 3: Computer Graphics – Transformation**

A triangle in the plane has vertices $A(1,1)$, $B(3,1)$, and $C(1,4)$. Points are written as column vectors. The triangle is rotated $90^\circ$ counterclockwise about the origin using the transformation matrix $R = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Find the images of $A$, $B$, and $C$ under the rotation.
(b) Compute the area of the triangle before and after rotation (using the matrix method, via determinant).
(c) Comment on how the transformation matrix affects the area and orientation.
explanation:
(a) Image of a point $P = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}$ is $R\cdot P$.

For $A(1,1)$:

$R \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \times 1 + (-1) \times 1 \\ 1 \times 1 + 0 \times 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$

For $B(3,1)$:

$R \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \times 3 + (-1) \times 1 \\ 1 \times 3 + 0 \times 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$

For $C(1,4)$:

$R \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \times 1 + (-1) \times 4 \\ 1 \times 1 + 0 \times 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$

(b) Area of triangle with points $P_1(x_1, y_1), P_2(x_2, y_2), P_3(x_3, y_3)$:

$A = \dfrac{1}{2} \left| \begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \right|$

Original triangle:

$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

Expand:

$1 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 \end{vmatrix} - 1 \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} + 1 \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 \end{vmatrix}$

$= 1(1 \times 1 - 1 \times 4) -1 (3 \times 1 - 1 \times 1) + 1 (3 \times 4 - 1 \times 1)$

$= 1(1-4) -1(3-1) +1(12-1)$

$= 1(-3) -1(2) + 1(11)$

$= -3 -2 + 11 = 6$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}|6| = 3$ units$^2$

After rotation: Vertices $( -1,1 ), ( -1,3 ), ( -4,1 )$

Determinant is:

$\begin{vmatrix} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 \\ -4 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

Expand:

$-1 \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} - 1 \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 1 \\ -4 & 1 \end{vmatrix} + 1 \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 3 \\ -4 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

$= -1(3-1) -1((-1 \times 1) - (1 \times -4)) + ((-1)(1)-3\times-4)$

$= -1(2)-1(-1+4)+(-1+12)$

$= -2 - 3 + 11 = 6$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} |6| = 3$ units$^2$

(c) The transformation matrix for rotation preserves area but changes the orientation. The determinant of $R$ is $+1$, so orientation is preserved. The absolute value of determinant gives the scale factor for area; since $| \det R | = 1$, the area remains unchanged.

options.A:
(a) $A'(1,-1)$, $B'(1,-3)$, $C'(4,-1)$.
(b) Area before rotation $=3$ square units and after rotation $=6$ square units.
(c) Since $\det R=-1$, area changes and orientation is reversed.
options.B:
(a) $A'(-1,1)$, $B'(-1,3)$, $C'(-4,1)$.
(b) Area before rotation $=3$ square units and after rotation $=3$ square units.
(c) Since $\det R=1$, the transformation preserves area and orientation.
options.C:
(a) $A'(1,1)$, $B'(3,1)$, $C'(1,4)$.
(b) Area before rotation $=6$ square units and after rotation $=6$ square units.
(c) Since $\det R=0$, the triangle collapses.
options.D:
(a) $A'(-1,-1)$, $B'(-3,-1)$, $C'(-1,-4)$.
(b) Area before rotation $=3$ square units and after rotation $=0$ square units.
(c) The transformation is not invertible.
